question.text: In which derivative market is the concept of 'cheapest-to-deliver' (CTD) bond relevant?

answer.text: Physically settled (notional) interest rate / bond futures — where the seller can choose which eligible bond from the deliverable basket to deliver and naturally picks the cheapest-to-deliver
Equity derivatives — where the seller delivers the cheapest stock from the index basket
Currency derivatives — where the seller delivers the cheapest currency pair
Commodity derivatives — where the seller delivers the lowest-grade commodity

explanation.text: The Logic: For physically settled notional-bond / interest-rate futures, the contract allows delivery of any bond from a basket of eligible deliverable bonds. The seller chooses the bond with the lowest effective delivery cost, known as the cheapest-to-deliver (CTD), with conversion factors used to standardise differences in coupon and maturity. The Trap: CTD is unique to physically settled bond/IR futures. Equity, currency, and commodity contracts in this exam scope are cash-settled (equity / currency) or have fixed delivery specifications (commodity) rather than a deliverable basket with seller choice. Note: The Interest Rate Derivatives workbook notes that at present all bond futures in India are cash-settled, and the physical-settlement section (where CTD lives) is included for study and reference. Yield movements change which deliverable bond is cheapest to deliver in those physically settled designs.
